column2: Palladium deliberately "poisoned" with lead so it stops halfway, turning alkynes into alkenes and no further. It sounds niche, but it's in every organic chemistry course.

A mix of copper and manganese oxides that turns poisonous carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide at room temperature, developed for gas masks in the First World War. Its name comes from the two universities behind it: Johns HOPkins and the University of CALifornia.

Walter Kaminsky found around 1980 that a trace of water turned a sluggish zirconium catalyst into one of the most active ever made for polyethylene, by forming a helper compound. The accident changed how plastics are made.
